claims.claim: The source-literal optimized FIFO algorithm’s complexity is Θ(n+M_FIFO), where M_FIFO=Σ_t|Q_t| for its actual marked queues; processing (p_t,Q_t) yields p_{t+1}=reverse(Q_t) followed by the stable deletion of Q_t from p_t.
claims.evidence: Write Q_t=(q_1,…,q_k). The source update rules maintain a duplicate-free queue of the current descent bottoms: deletion-created adjacencies are tested before moving an element, while each newly created front adjacency is tested before MoveToFront. Processing q_1,…,q_k successively prepends them, so induction gives the prefix (q_k,…,q_1), while every unqueued element retains its relative order. Initialization scans Θ(n) entries. Each queued element causes Θ(1) comparisons and list/queue operations, and the number of nonempty rounds is at most M_FIFO; hence both the upper and lower operation counts are Θ(n+M_FIFO). The exact checker also verified the queue-set and transition invariants on every run for all permutations through n=9.
claims.search_method: Direct invariant proof, direct source-pseudocode transcription, exhaustive transition checks through n=9, and deterministic exact stress tests for n=10,…,40.

claims.claim: There is an exact phase decomposition that isolates the unresolved cost.
claims.evidence: If i is the largest unfixed value, all larger values occupy a permanent fixed suffix; therefore i lies at a position s_i<i and cannot be a descent bottom or queue member. Relative side with respect to i is unchanged until a queued element is processed. Removing an element left of i shifts i left once and prepending it shifts i right once, for net zero. Removing an element right of i does not shift i, while prepending it advances i once. Thus one round advances i by exactly q_t. While i is not fixed, its immediate right neighbor is smaller and marked, so q_t≥1; summing until fixation gives Σ_tq_t=i−s_i. Since the phase processes Σ_t(ℓ_t+q_t) elements, its exact move count is (i−s_i)+Σ_tℓ_t. The second term is not bounded more sharply by the argument.
claims.search_method: Deductive position-change proof, supplemented by exhaustive exact phase-invariant checks over all 409,113 permutations of sizes 1 through 9 and 3,100 deterministic exact stress runs of sizes 10 through 40.

claims.claim: The parent does not establish an Ω(n^{3/2}) lower bound, or the coefficient (4√2/3+o(1)), for the source-literal optimized FIFO algorithm.
claims.evidence: The concrete transfer identity used by the described staircase argument is false. Starting from P_6=(6,1,2,3,4,5), three ordinary shelf-order transitions give (3,1,2,6,4,5), whereas three source-literal FIFO rounds give (1,3,2,6,4,5). Thus a recurrence proved for the ordinary T orbit does not count the literal FIFO orbit. No independent transfer or replacement lower-bound proof is supplied, so the stated Ω(n^{3/2}) bound and coefficient are not established. This does not show that such a lower bound is false.
claims.search_method: Exact side-by-side execution of the ordinary descent-bottom transition and the source-literal detection-ordered FIFO pseudocode.

claims.claim: For n≤9, the exact maximum numbers of moves for the source-literal optimized FIFO algorithm are 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53.
claims.evidence: Exhaustive lexicographic enumeration covered all Σ_{n=1}^9 n!=409,113 permutations. A direct vector transcription and an independent array-backed doubly-linked-list transcription agreed on every terminal shelf, move count, and round count. The resulting maxima were exactly 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53. All executions terminated sorted, and no duplicate queue entries were observed.
claims.search_method: Complete exact enumeration with two independently represented implementations; all counters and comparisons were integral.

claims.claim: A natural twice-per-unordered-pair charging bound is false.
claims.evidence: For the stated 4096-element permutation, exact literal FIFO execution makes 49,545,006 moves. A charging scheme assigning at most two moves to each unordered pair could cover at most 2·binom(4096,2)=4096·4095=16,773,120 moves. Since 49,545,006>16,773,120, that bound is impossible for every execution. The check also confirmed the supporting distinction: P_13 has 97 literal moves versus 161 ordinary-T moves, while the 4096 witness has 50,546,772 ordinary-T moves. This finite counterexample does not refute an O(n²) bound with another constant.
claims.search_method: Exact O(1)-per-move array-backed doubly-linked-list simulation, with integer counters and a separate exact ordinary-transition implementation.

claims.claim: The requested asymptotically tight worst-case step complexity remains unresolved; this revision establishes no improvement beyond the source’s Ω(n log n)–O(n³) interval.
claims.evidence: The authorized source gives Ω(n log n) and O(n³). Claim 0 merely reparameterizes the cost by the uncontrolled quantity M_FIFO. Claim 1 leaves Σ_tℓ_t uncontrolled. Claim 2 withdraws rather than replaces the proposed asymptotic lower bound. Claims 3 and 4 are finite computations and supply neither an asymptotic family nor an n-only estimate. The phase argument recovers termination and at most O(n³), but nothing tighter: an active value i has at most i−1 rounds and at most i queued moves per round, whose sum over i is O(n³). Thus no matching or improved asymptotic bound is established by the revision.
claims.search_method: Dependency audit of every proved statement against the exact requested n-asymptotic target and the authorized source bounds.
